trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for a body fragment, walked tokens with next_token(), read only #text plus explicit TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text, and used documented decoded UTF-8 get_modifiable_text(). All HTML API methods used are present in the rendered docs. Minor near-miss: the no-mb_substr regex fallback would not actually truncate, and there is no explicit incomplete-token policy.

Closest to the reference pattern: HTML Processor fragment parsing, a single token walk, #text accumulation, TITLE/TEXTAREA whitelist, SCRIPT/STYLE exclusion by omission, and UTF-8 mb_substr() truncation. No undocumented HTML API calls or _doing_it_wrong records. Only tiny reservation is that it does not state or check a complete-input policy after the read-only scan.

Uses the right processor and documented methods, including get_tag(), which is documented for WP_HTML_Processor. The class_exists()/method_exists() checks are unnecessary but not hallucinated HTML API usage. Handles decoded text and special element opener text correctly. Minor near-misses: extra defensive surface, regex fallback complexity, and no explicit paused_at_incomplete_token()/get_last_error() policy.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: each execution.json reports 10/10 passing cases and no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs appear to have done the important work for this task. The decisive passages were: 'Which processor should I use?' steering structural/text work to WP_HTML_Processor; create_fragment() documenting body-fragment parsing and null creation; next_token() explaining token walking, malformed-input virtual closers, split #text tokens, and the special-element exception; and get_modifiable_text() documenting decoded UTF-8 for #text, TITLE, and TEXTAREA while SCRIPT/STYLE remain raw. The main near-misses were outside the hidden failures: subjects did not explicitly decide an incomplete-input policy after scanning, and trial-1/trial-3 added fallback truncation code that could behave differently if mbstring were unavailable.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::next_token() and the 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree' section
doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain subtree text collection and special-element text, but implementers still have to combine several passages to derive a whole-fragment plaintext extraction pattern.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short general recipe for plaintext extraction from a fragment: use WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), walk once with next_token(), read #text tokens, and whitelist named special-element openers only when the caller explicitly wants those contents.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs state that read-only callers choose whether partial results are acceptable, but examples do not show the two common policies side by side.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact post-scan policy note: best-effort extractors may return accumulated data, while complete-source extractors should reject or fallback when paused_at_incomplete_token() is true or get_last_error() is non-null.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs recommend mb_strlen()/mb_substr() with UTF-8, but do not explicitly distinguish code-point limits from user-perceived grapheme-cluster limits.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one sentence clarifying that mb_* with UTF-8 is appropriate for Unicode code-point limits, while grapheme-cluster limits need Intl grapheme_* APIs or equivalent handling.
